 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANISH DAYAL  ORDER % 19.04.2023 CRL.M.A. 10221/2023 (Exemption)
1. Exemption is allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application is disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed for quashing of the FIR No.450/2018 registered under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC at PS Malviya Nagar, New Delhi, on the ground of a settlement between the parties dated 24.12.2022, which is on record of this Court.
2. Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 and respondent No.2/complainant are present in Court, duly identified by their counsel and the IO.
As per the settlement, an amount of Rs.10 Lakhs has been agreed as full and final settlement to be paid to respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 states that she has received an amount of Rs.5,20,000/- at the stage of first motion, which has been concluded, Rs.3 Lakhs vide a DD bearing No.639749 dated 08.12.2022 has been paid to her today, which she has duly received and
as per the settlement, the balance amount of Rs.1,80,000/- is to be paid at the time of recording of the statement in the second motion.
The learned counsels for the parties state that the second motion has already been filed.
Respondent No.2 has no objection to the quashing of the said FIR in terms of the settlement.
The FIR is accordingly being quashed on the basis of the settlement

,
however, it is made clear that it is conditional upon the compliance of the terms of the settlement arrived at between the parties.
3. The petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 were married on 20.03.2017 and one female child was born out of the wedlock.
4. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR Rahul & Ors vs State Of Nct Delhi & Anr on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5669256/
1 as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.450/2018 registered under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC at PS Malviya Nagar, New Delhi, and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
It is however made clear that the said settlement will not affect the rights of the minor child in future.
5. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications, if any, are disposed of as infructuous.
6. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J APRIL 19, 2023/kct Rahul & Ors vs State Of Nct Delhi & Anr on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5669256/
